findings.where: KO sentence 7 (and KO 9 clause '#348 holds heteronyms not masks')
findings.finding: #348's stipulation is scoped to the archive's own framework; the KO drops the qualifier 'within the NH-OS framework' and composes it as a general definition of the heteronym ('The archive defines the heteronym as a function: heteronyms "are not pseudonyms, masks, or personas"'). Dropping a qualifier raises the claim (§5.3). The source's own text confirms the scope (AXN-0098 line 20, under the subtitle 'Authorial Emergence, Exhaust, and Excess within NH-OS').
findings.evidence: N348-01 quote: "Heteronyms within the NH-OS framework are not pseudonyms, masks, or personas."
findings.fix: KO 7: 'Within the archive's own framework, NH-OS, #348 holds that heteronyms "are not pseudonyms, masks, or personas" but "**authorial functions**", authorship treated "as a system, not a name"; for #79 a heteronym is ...'. KO 9: '#348 holds the heteronyms of NH-OS not masks'.

findings.where: KO sentence 7, opening clause
findings.finding: 'The archive defines the heteronym as a function' credits the definition to the archive as a whole. KO 9 then shows the archive's deposits disagree on exactly this point (#96 'A heteronym is a person.'), and the row status lists person/position as contested within the pool. The subject should be the deposits that state it (§4.5).
findings.evidence: N96-02 quote: "A heteronym is a person."; N90-02 quote: "The heteronyms are not separate persons; they are differentiated positions"
findings.fix: Replace 'The archive defines the heteronym as a function:' with '#348 and #79 define the heteronym as a function:'.

findings.where: KO sentence 35, clause 'in Pessoa "The master position is constituted by dying.", as "The death of a heteronym is not failure. It is formal completion." (#348)'
findings.finding: The 'as' makes #348's NH-OS principle the explanation of Caeiro's death in Pessoa. No cited quote states that link. #348 is about heteronyms within NH-OS ('A new voice inherits what survives'), and #1572 [H2] gives Pessoa's case a different bearing: its heading reads 'AND THE DEATH OF THE MASTER IS NOT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE' (AXN-0664 line 364). The join is the composer's coordinating act, it is not logged (§4.7), and it fails reverse entailment.
findings.evidence: N1572-02 context, AXN-0664: "[H2] AND THE DEATH OF THE MASTER IS NOT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE. Pessoa gives Caeiro a lifespan ... The master position is constituted by dying."; N348-04 context, AXN-0098 line 27: "The death of a heteronym is not failure. It is formal completion. The archive seals. A new voice inherits what survives."
findings.fix: Split into two clauses: 'in Pessoa, #1572 finds, "The master position is constituted by dying."; and #348 states, of heteronyms within NH-OS, that "The death of a heteronym is not failure. It is formal completion."'. Optionally carry [H2]'s 'not independent evidence' bearing at the next ledger revision (it is not in the ledger now).

findings.where: KO sentence 14
findings.finding: Several clauses name no source (§4.5): the opening Caeiro clause (F51, B8 Poetry International), 'they "collaborated on projects ..."' (F20, B2 Poetry Society) and '"There was considerable interaction among the heteronyms"' (F52, B8). The only parenthetical naming Poetry International is attached to the last clause (F53). A reader would credit F51 to no one and F20 to Wikipedia.
findings.evidence: F51 (B8 ¶2): "Caeiro, the first in the poetic trinity to emerge from Pessoa’s soul, was considered the Master of the other two and, indeed, of Pessoa himself."; F20 (B2 body): "They also collaborated on projects (Crosse worked with his brother, I. I. Crosse)"; F52 (B8 ¶5)

findings.where: P lede; P 'What it is' items 'The field:' and 'The archive:'; P items 'Positions:', '1914:', 'Interplay:', 'Counts:'
findings.finding: The compression attributes to ledger families ('The field gives it ...; the archive defines it ...'; labels 'The field:', 'The archive:'), and several items carry no source at all. A family is not a source (§4.5). The family split also brings back the field/archive division that the equal-terms lede is meant to compose away (§5.8: 'the definition composed from both ledgers').
findings.evidence: P lede: "The field gives it its own supposed physique, biography and style; the archive defines it as an authorial function, attributable through its civil bearer and not reducible to it."
findings.fix: Lede: '... its own supposed physique, biography and style (Wikipedia); an authorial function, attributable through its civil bearer and not reducible to it (#940).' Rename the labels by content ('A character:', 'A position:') and name the source in each item, e.g. 'Interplay: they criticise, translate and meddle in Pessoa's life (Wikipedia, Poetry International)'; 'Positions: ... (Wikipedia; Lopes and later critics, #667)'.

findings.where: KO paragraphs 6–10 (sentences 22–35) against paragraph 3 (sentences 13–15); translation rows 6 and 7
findings.finding: The §5.10 breach does not occur (0 of 10 KO_B sentences survive). But the last fourteen sentences are an archive-only run (KO 26's Bowie clause, F14, is the one field claim), and several of those archive claims are about the field's own objects. N1570-03 says Caeiro's epithet '*the master*' is supplied by Mora, Campos and Reis, against F6, F37 and F51 (Caeiro the master). N1570-05/06 (a configuration instantiating master–student) bear on F5 and F20 (the heteronyms interacting). N1572-02 (Caeiro's master position constituted by dying) and N682-03 (Orpheu 1915) bear on the 1914 sense. These sit in paragraphs 6 and 10, not beside the field claims they bear on, so the archive's measured senses close the KO as a block (§4.1, §4.7: ordered together by sense). The translation table itself says F6/F37/F51 are 'composed as received beside N1561-01, N1572-02, N1570-03', and F5/F12/F20/F52/F34/F53 'beside N1570-05, N1570-06, N667-05'. The KO's arrangement does not do this, so the plan and the text disagree.
findings.evidence: translation row 6: "untranslated: composed as received beside N1561-01, N1572-02, N1570-03"; N1570-03: "Every term by which Caeiro is known is ABSENT from Caeiro. Paganism, sensationism, objectivism, the master, sensibility — all supplied by Mora, Campos and Reis."
findings.fix: Move the N1570-03 clause and the N1572-02 clause into KO 14, after the Caeiro-as-master clauses, and the N1570-05/06 clause after the interaction clauses. Move N682-03 (Orpheu) into KO 13 beside N682-08. Keep KO 32–34's method and limit claims (N1560-03, N1570-01/02, N1572-04) where they are. Alternatively, amend translation rows 6–7 to match the KO as composed, and log the arrangement.

findings.where: case / ρ
findings.finding: All 10 case loci are verbatim in the named texts (checked mechanically, 10/10). Equal-terms with ρ = extends is supported. #667 and #682 present themselves as formalizing and extending Pessoa's own typology, and #666 says cross-substrate practice 'does not violate the typological structure'. The archive's sharpest contests (formalized, not invented; a heteronym is a person) have counterparts in B3 (F26, F31 on Yeats; F27 'a real man ... except ... being real itself'), so §0.10 does not apply. A reader of the same papers might weigh the Plato–Aristotle configuration (#123, #136, #1658) as a witness-type ontology, since it rules at the Theophrastus row. At this entity, though, #123 marks it 'an analytic category, not a claim about historical self-description', and #136/#1658 apply the category to antiquity without redefining the heteronym. I would decide equal.
findings.evidence: #123 §II: "It is crucial to mark that this is an analytic category, not a claim about historical self-description."; #666 §5: "The substrate dimension adds a new variable but does not violate the typological structure."
findings.fix: None.

summary: The literary-heteronym composition largely holds. All 256 quoted fragments in the KO and P are verbatim in the ledger quotes they cite. All 190 ledger claims (55 field, 135 archive) are carried in the KO, with no cuts. Every field claim is in exactly one translation row with its quote verbatim. The 10 case loci are verbatim and support equal / ρ = extends. One must-fix: #348's NH-OS scope is dropped (KO 7, 9). Should-fixes: attribution in KO 14 and the compression; the #348–Pessoa join in KO 35; the archive's measured claims on Caeiro and the master–student relation sit in a closing archive run, away from the field claims the translation table says they stand beside; P raises Steiner's 'not rare' and miscredits 'partial heteronyms' to #667; 8 kernels are not verifiable on the compression.
